title: Urgent service degradation — spokes notes and Q&A (standby)
content:
Purpose: quick-reference spokes notes and Q&A for managers on standby while we triage degraded serving in us-west-2. This is a personal scratchpad — short, blunt, editable.

Key principles to keep in all comms:
- Acknowledge quickly, be factual, avoid speculation.
- Reassure with observable actions (teams, mitigation steps, ETA windows).
- Surface customer impact clearly (who, how many requests, which APIs/routes).
- Commit to follow-up: timeline for next update and postmortem cadence.

Suggested Slack announcement (short, sent by @ravi or @oncall):
"Heads up — we're seeing degraded latency and increased errors for text-generation routes in us-west-2 (hosted API). Engineering is investigating. If you're experiencing failed requests, please retry after ~30s. We'll post updates every 15–30 minutes and share a postmortem. Incident key: JIRA-INC-4312."

Longer note for internal channel or email to CS/GTM leads: (copyable)
- What happened: starting ~09:12 PDT we observed 5xx spikes and P95 token latency > 3s for /v1/generate and chat endpoints in us-west-2. Traffic reduction measures were auto-triggered but errors continued for a subset of model variants.
- Impact: ~12% of requests for enterprise customers in region, intermittent client-visible failures and timeouts. No data exfiltration indicators.
- Current mitigation: routing fallback to compatible model pool in us-east-1 for critical customers, partial capacity scaling for dedicated pools, and rolling restart of serving nodes in the affected cluster.
- Who's on it: eng-sre (oncall Ravi), serving-runtime (Diego), infra (Asha), platform-engineering (TBD).
- Next update: 09:45 PDT. Postmortem planned within 72 hours.

All-hands talking points (if asked by managers):
- Short: We found an unexpected degradation in our serving cluster in us-west-2. We're actively mitigating and routing critical traffic to healthy regions. Customers should see improving success rates within the hour.
- If pressed on root cause: still investigating. Early signs point to a combination of resource exhaustion on a new autoscaling path + a model variant that reverted to a heavier quantization fallback under load. Will confirm in postmortem.
- If asked about SLA: We're treating this as a high-severity operational incident. CS should log impacted accounts; we'll evaluate credits/compensation on a case-by-case basis after the postmortem.
- If leadership asks about notification timing: We escalated internally as soon as we had correlated telemetry and started rerouting. Public customer-facing comms should be coordinated with CS and legal.

Manager Q&A cheat sheet (common Qs and short answers):
Q: How long until traffic normalized?
A: Expected stabilization within 30–90 minutes after current reroutes and node restarts; we'll update timeline as we validate recovery.

Q: Are any customers at risk of data loss or corruption?
A: No evidence of data loss. This is a latency/error surface issue. All requests are retried where applicable and logs/KV are intact.

Q: Should we proactively reach out to customers?
A: CS should proactively reach out to customers with known SLAs and those who reported errors. Use the internal template (link in linked_artifacts). For others, wait for the next all-clear — don't share unconfirmed root cause.

Q: Do we need to pause new rollouts or config changes?
A: Yes — pause any serving runtime rollouts in us-west-2 and any autoscaling config flips until investigative signal clears. Use canary elsewhere only.

What not to say (quick guardrails):
- Do not speculate about security breach unless confirmed by SecOps.
- Avoid committing to compensation amounts or SLA changes on the spot.
- Avoid naming internal engineers publicly. Use team names only.

Triage checklist (notes to self):
- Confirm scope: dashboards -> errors by route, model variant, customer. (Diego)
- Force routing of premium customers to us-east-1 pool and monitor error delta. (Asha)
- Validate autoscaling thresholds and recent commits to scaling logic. (oncall)
- Preserve logs: snapshot cluster logs + kernel/driver traces for nodes that showed memory pressure. (infra)
- Open postmortem doc and start timeline. Template: include impact, timeline, RCA, mitigations, follow-ups.

Draft post-incident items (for later):
- Track whether quantization fallback logic needs a safety-check under autoscaling.
- Add a canary job that simulates sustained high-concurrency on new autoscale path.
- Improve route-level observability: surface model-variant fallback counts as an alerting metric.

Open questions (to resolve in next 24–48h):
- Did a recent model onboarding change default variant assignment for legacy customers? (Investigate onboarding PRs)
- Exact sequence that led to node memory pressure — kernel OOM or user-space leak?
- Are there any customers who retried in a way that caused duplicate billing? (billing to coordinate)

Notes to self / quick edits:
- Keep announcement short; link to internal incident channel and JIRA.
- Prep a single slide for later all-hands with timeline + top 3 action items.
- Loop in legal if any customer requests for early disclosure.

Scratch / ideas for follow-up comms:
- Customer-facing post (once cause known): short apology + clear remediation + what we'll change.
- Internal thank-you note after incident resolved: highlight triage owners + concrete follow-ups assigned.

TODO (items I will do in next 60 minutes):
- Post the short Slack announcement in ops-incident and cs-alerts (09:18).
- Trigger routing to us-east-1 for critical accounts (09:22).
- Ping platform-engineering for temporary capacity bump (09:25).

— end of scratchpad —

(If I leave this doc and return: mark resolved when primary error rate <1% and P95 latency within normal bounds for 10m window.)
